key_insight: Surrogate-guided agentic search finds low-energy atomic orderings in site-disordered crystals more reliably and with fewer costly evaluations than traditional search methods.
engineering_relevance: The framework can reduce the structural-relaxation workload needed to model chemically disordered crystalline materials.
method: Fit a surrogate to evaluated configurations and select new candidates by balancing exploitation, uncertainty, and novelty.
Compare ExtraTrees, Bayesian ridge, sparse ARD, and an ALiEGNN-inspired graph ensemble against three traditional search methods.
Encode coupled Na/vacancy and Fe charge-state disorder to model Na2/3FePO4.
evidence_signal: Across 14 test cases spanning 12 crystal structures with exhaustively verified global minima, agentic surrogates succeeded in 94% of runs versus 55% for traditional methods, with a median 4.3-fold reduction in evaluations relative to the best traditional method.
watch_item: Performance on larger, non-enumerable search spaces remains unverified; recovering the reported Na2/3FePO4 ordering required explicit charge-state encoding.
paper_title: Agentic Global Optimization of Site-Disordered Crystalline Materials
